t: Maximum Font to Fit a Sentence in a Screen
o: We must pick the largest font size from a sorted list such that the text's total width fits within `w` and its height (same for all characters at that size) fits within `h`. Since both width and height grow monotonically with font size, feasibility is monotonic: if size S fits, every smaller size fits. That monotonicity is exactly what binary search over the fonts array exploits. In Example 1, sizes 8+ make the text too wide, so 6 is the answer; in Example 2, size 4 fits comfortably; in Example 3, even the smallest size 10 exceeds the screen, giving -1. With text up to 50,000 chars and up to 100,000 font sizes, checking every size naively costs O(n·m) = 5×10⁹ operations — too slow — while binary search needs only O(n log m) calls to FontInfo.
k: Feasibility is monotone in font size: if a size fits, all smaller sizes fit, enabling binary search.
Check height first (O(1) call) before summing widths, since it can reject a candidate instantly.
Cache character widths per font size during a check to avoid recomputing getWidth for repeated characters.

a.i: Try each font size from largest to smallest and return the first one that fits. This directly mirrors the problem statement and works because fonts are sorted. It is simple but does O(n) work per candidate, which can be too slow when many sizes are feasible or nearly feasible.
s: Iterate fonts from the last index down to 0.
For each size, first compare getHeight(size) with h; if taller, continue.
Sum getWidth(size, ch) over all characters of text; early-exit if the running sum exceeds w.
If the total width is at most w, return this size.
a.t: O(n · m) worst case where n = |text| and m = number of fonts, though early exits help in practice.

a.i: Because width and height are non-decreasing in font size, 'fits' is a prefix property over the sorted fonts array: all fitting sizes form a contiguous prefix. Binary search for the boundary — the last index whose size fits — in O(log m) checks, each costing O(n).
s: While lo <= hi, mid = (lo + hi) / 2; check fonts[mid].
A size fits iff getHeight(size) <= h and the summed width of text at that size is <= w (early-exit once the sum exceeds w).
If it fits, record ans = mid and search the right half (lo = mid + 1); otherwise search the left half (hi = mid - 1).
a.t: O(n log m) — each of the O(log m) binary-search steps scans the text once (with early exit on overflow).
a.sp: O(1) extra space beyond the input.

w: In an interview, mention the linear scan briefly, then pivot immediately to binary search by pointing out the monotonicity guarantee given in the statement. Pitfalls: forgetting the height check (it is O(1) and can prune instantly), overflowing the width sum in fixed-width languages (use 64-bit or rely on early exit), and returning the index instead of the font value. Edge cases: no size fits (return -1), only the smallest size fits, and single-character text. Follow-ups might ask to minimize FontInfo calls further (e.g., precompute per-character counts and cache widths per probed size), or how the approach changes if text could wrap across multiple lines.
